claims.head: Who blinks first?
claims.body: The Oilers are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Panthers are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Oilers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years. The Panthers take a lot of penalties, so the Oilers’ power play should get its chances.

story.head: Who blinks first?
paras: The Panthers have won two in a row, and the Oilers have won three straight. Going in, the Oilers are first in the Pacific (third in the NHL) and the Cats fifth in the Atlantic (13th).

The Oilers’ record (.775) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.574), largely thanks to their finishing. The Panthers’ record (.600) is about what their chances are worth. If the Oilers’ record were closer to their chances, like the Panthers’, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Oilers lean on their stars more than any team in the league (lowest) and ice the puck less than almost anyone (2nd). They also have one of the league’s most dangerous power plays (2nd), and their power play against the Panthers’ penalty killers is strength against strength. Edmonton has scored 4.00 goals a game, the third most in the league. On the other side, the Panthers forecheck harder than anyone (1st), hit a lot (1st) and don't block many shots (32nd). Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Connor McDavid (11 G / 38 A / 49 P in 20 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with ten points in his last five games. Leon Draisaitl (18 G / 19 A / 37 P in 20 GP) has a team-high 18 goals, the most in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games. Matthew Tkachuk (4 G / 24 A / 28 P in 20 GP) leads the Panthers in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. Sam Reinhart (11 G / 8 A / 19 P in 20 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, with a point in five straight games against Edmonton.
Devon Levi (8-1-0 / .898 SV% in 9 GS) will likely start for Edmonton, and Jacob Markström (5-3-1 / .900 SV% in 10 GS) for Florida.
At home, Paul Maurice likes to send Luostarinen, Lundell and Vilmanis out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Podkolzin, McDavid and Draisaitl.
